findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL storage, snapshots and backups unencrypted, exposing all stored data if the underlying storage or a snapshot copy is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance an internet-routable endpoint (also exported as a Terraform output), massively expanding attack surface for credential brute force and engine exploitation.
The master username is the default, predictable value 'admin', which combined with the public endpoint and static password authentication makes credential-guessing attacks materially easier.

The master password comes from var.password, which is persisted in plaintext in Terraform state and is additionally interpolated into EC2 user data, creating multiple credential disclosure paths for a publicly reachable database.

findings.issue_category: no IAM auth or audit logging
findings.description: IAM database authentication and CloudWatch log exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) are not enabled, so access to an internet-facing database relies solely on a shared static password with no database-level audit trail.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible instance accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/query data can be intercepted in transit.

user_data interpolates the DB username and var.password in cleartext and writes them to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF, and is stored unencrypted in the instance description.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving IMDSv1 enabled. An SSRF flaw in the PHP application would yield both the plaintext user data (DB password) and credentials for an instance profile holding s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*.
No root_block_device encryption is configured, so the volume storing the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file may be written unencrypted at rest.
The bootstrap installs httpd/PHP serving the employee data form over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration, so submitted personal data and any session material travel in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web instance. Compromise of that host yields account-wide data access, resource control and privilege-escalation paths (e.g. ec2:RunInstances with PassRole).
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, enabling unconstrained outbound traffic for data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised host.

Port 3306 ingress is allowed from the whole VPC CIDR rather than being scoped to the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database directly; this is the only network boundary protecting a publicly accessible RDS instance.
